solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Musical entertainment for millions

parts.note: pro means in favour of, so 'for' gives PRO
M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A concert or show that pulls in an audience of millions.
explanation.walkthrough: A PROM is a promenade concert, as in the BBC Proms, the London summer classical season.
explanation.definitionFit: A promenade concert is a performance of music, so it is a kind of musical entertainment.

clue.text: What's in store, having finally found a boyfriend?

definitions.meaning: goods ready-made and stocked in a shop, available to buy at once
a woman left unmarried is said to be 'on the shelf', so one who finds a partner is no longer there

explanation.surface: A shop question merged with a lonely woman's happy news about at last finding a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the shelf' is an old idiom for someone thought past the age of marrying; the question mark flags the playful reversal of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock goods sit on a shop's racks ready for purchase; a romance takes someone out of the idiomatic spinsterhood.

clue.text: Possibly greasy food in reserve

parts.note: grub is informal for food
something put by is kept in reserve, so 'by' carries that sense

explanation.surface: Some oily snack being kept back for later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks greasy as just one way of being dirty, a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grubby is dirty, and grease is one kind of grime that makes it so.

clue.text: Exonerating unruly children of the 1970s

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters of the word before are put in disorder

explanation.surface: Clearing the name of badly behaved youngsters born in the seventies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exonerating' looks like the verb of the sentence but is only the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The cohort label for people born roughly from the mid-1960s to around 1980, following the baby boomers.

clue.text: Mother's brother Bill fails to get Megane finally out of gear

indicators.note: failing to get something means it is missing, so that letter is left out

parts.note: a mother's brother is an uncle

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word Megane

parts.note: an ad (advertisement) is a bill posted up

explanation.surface: A relative called Bill cannot shift his Renault Megane out of gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of gear' reads as motoring, but gear here is clothing; the Megane is a Renault car model and gives only its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear is slang for clothes, so being without it means naked or undressed.

clue.text: Bishop threatening to be fresh?

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
something looming hangs over you menacingly

explanation.surface: A churchman with menace in mind seems likely to get cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' tempts as cheeky, but it means flourishing, as flowers do; the question mark warns of the shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers in bloom are at their freshest and healthiest, so the word describes vigorous, flourishing growth.

clue.text: Champion returned

definitions.meaning: to champion a cause is to support it
came home again, arrived again where one started

explanation.definitionFit: To back someone is to support them; someone who is back has come home again.

clue.text: Banker initially given responsibility for extra pay

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word Banker

parts.note: an onus is a burden of duty or responsibility

explanation.surface: A banker entrusted with duties gets an additional payment, a dig at City bonus culture.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is a payment over and above normal wages or salary.

clue.text: Company embracing radical set of beliefs

indicators.note: embracing means holding within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: red is used for a left-wing radical

explanation.surface: A firm adopting extreme political principles.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed or statement of faith, from the Latin for 'I believe'.

clue.text: Weapon seen a lot around Lima

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece is placed outside the other

parts.note: something rife is widespread and seen everywhere
Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A gun often spotted in the Peruvian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Lima looks like Peru's capital but stands for L, its code word in the radio alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-barrelled gun with a grooved bore, fired from the shoulder.

clue.text: Person to raise spirits playing Amen Corner round clubs

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the jumbled letters wrap the other piece
playing here means fooling about with, so the band's name is jumbled

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Someone cheering people up by playing Amen Corner records around the nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Amen Corner were a 1960s British pop group; 'raise spirits' suggests cheering up, but means summoning the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorcerer who conjures the dead to foretell the future literally raises ghosts.

clue.text: Peculiar item adorning leader of religion?

definitions.text: Peculiar item adorning leader of religion?

indicators.note: adorning means decorating around, so the jumbled letters enclose the other piece
peculiar means odd, so the word item is rearranged
the leader of a word is its first letter, here of religion

explanation.surface: A strange object decorating a church leader's head.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a bishop's tall hat is an odd-looking thing worn by a church leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall pointed headdress worn by bishops is a striking ornament on a senior cleric.

clue.text: Register with embassy getting let back in

parts.note: a meter or gauge reads, that is registers, a value
a diplomatic mission is an embassy

explanation.surface: Signing in with a diplomatic office to be allowed back into a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Register' looks like signing in, but means show a reading, as a dial does.
explanation.definitionFit: Being admitted again after leaving or being expelled; the noun names that act of re-entry.

clue.text: Peter dashes off something on a computer

indicators.note: off means out of order or wrong, so the letters before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Peter hurriedly writes a quick note on his laptop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dashes off' reads as writing quickly; 'off' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A program laying out figures in rows and columns, run on a PC; a vague definition by example.

clue.text: Help for TV presenters — radio bods will get confused with it

indicators.note: getting confused means being mixed up, so these letters are scrambled together

explanation.surface: Radio staff are baffled by the autocue gadgets of television.
explanation.walkthrough: Bods is British slang for people; the fodder is the two words before the indicator plus 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Boards held off-camera showing a presenter the script, an early form of autocue or prompter.

clue.text: Rugby score ruled out? Engage a lawyer

indicators.note: to engage is to take in, so the first piece holds the second inside

parts.note: a try is a rugby score; one disallowed by the referee is a 'no try'

explanation.surface: After a disputed try is disallowed, someone decides to hire legal help.
explanation.definitionFit: A public official who certifies documents and witnesses signatures, a type of legal practitioner.

clue.text: Top man perhaps for a laugh round North Carolina

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the laugh wraps the state abbreviation

parts.note: ho ho is the written sound of a hearty laugh
NC is the US postal abbreviation for North Carolina

explanation.surface: The boss goes to North Carolina just to have some fun.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal American word for the boss or leader of an organisation; 'perhaps' because a woman can be one too.

clue.text: First stages where films are shot

definitions.meaning: filming takes place ..., on the studio's built scenery

explanation.definitionFit: Beginnings are starts; movie scenes are filmed on studio stages built for the purpose.

clue.text: Infiltrator — one penetrating in French meeting

parts.note: en is French for in

indicators.note: penetrating means getting inside, so the numeral goes into the meeting word

parts.note: a tryst is a secret meeting, often of lovers
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A spy who slips into a French gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who joins a political party to subvert it from within, as Militant did with Labour.

clue.text: Increase fortification endlessly anticipating the French

indicators.note: anticipating means coming before, so the shortened fort precedes the article
endlessly means without its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a redoubt is a small fortified outwork
le is a French word for the

explanation.surface: Military talk of strengthening a fort before the French arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Increase fortification' looks like one phrase, but the definition is only the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: To redouble efforts is to intensify them, making them greater, a verb sense of growth.

clue.text: Early American rustic hero keeping masks

indicators.note: masks means conceals, so the answer lies hidden inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A country-bred hero who keeps a collection of masks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'masks' looks like a noun being kept; it is a verb meaning hides.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American people, so among the original inhabitants of America, long before the colonists.

clue.text: Who will give instructions to pack up

definitions.text: Who will give instructions to pack up

parts.words: Who will give instructions to pack up
parts.note: a pack of hunting dogs is directed by the person in charge of the hunt, who also urges them on; 'pack up' sounds like quitting

explanation.walkthrough: 'pack up' reads as stopping work or packing bags, but the pack is a group of hunting hounds and 'up' is them getting going.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a fox hunt controls the hounds and directs the hunt staff.

clue.text: Lag during match

parts.note: in, as in 'in the night', means during
to mate is to pair or match up

explanation.surface: A slowdown in the middle of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lag' looks like a delay but is British slang for a convict, as in 'old lag'.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-serving convict is an old lag, so a lag is a prisoner.

clue.text: See 20
Fast walkers keep in line

indicators.note: keep in means hold inside, so the walking word holds the line letter

parts.note: feet are what we walk with

explanation.surface: Speedy hikers stay in single file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast walkers' reads as quick hikers, but the definition is 'Fast' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet of foot means swift; the adjective describes rapid movement.

clue.text: Decimal points being removed from this won't change meaning a lot

definitions.text: Decimal points being removed from this won't change meaning a lot

parts.words: Decimal points being removed from this won't change meaning a lot
parts.note: the answer ends in ten, a decimal; strip its compass points E and N and the shorter word left still means frequently

explanation.walkthrough: 'Decimal points' suggests the dots in numbers; here the points are compass letters inside the word for ten, and 'a lot' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Frequently, many times; the shortened poetic form oft means the same.

clue.text: Tried assiduously to reserve energy

indicators.note: to reserve is to keep back, held inside, so the energy letter goes within

parts.note: to work hard is to work assiduously
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone made a great effort to save their strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tried' looks like 'attempted', but in the legal sense a court has heard a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A case that has been tried in court has been heard by the judge or jury.

clue.text: Dreadful person running company? Not half

indicators.note: not half means only part, so just the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: a director runs a company

explanation.surface: An awful boss who is only half up to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is also British slang for 'very much', a handy disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire straits are terrible ones; the adjective means appalling or very bad.

clue.text: He investigated rude message about poet

parts.note: a sext is a sexually explicit text message
on means concerning, about
William Blake was an English poet

explanation.surface: Someone looked into an obscene text concerning a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Sexton Blake is a British fictional detective, long popular in boys' magazines and comics.
explanation.definitionFit: A fictional private detective, so a character who carried out investigations.

clue.text: Bush, G. H. W. relative to G. W.?

definitions.meaning: a shrub with white flowers and dark berries

definitions.text: G. H. W. relative to G. W.?
definitions.meaning: George H. W. Bush is the father of George W. Bush, the senior of the two

explanation.walkthrough: The 'Bush' name ties both halves: the shrub sense and the two presidents named Bush.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a shrub; the father is the older of two family members.

clue.text: Crackers brought back are amazing

definitions.note: a plural verb phrase: things that astonish are things that amaze

indicators.note: brought back means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: crackers and nuts both mean mad

explanation.surface: Christmas crackers being brought back are wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crackers' suggests the festive novelty but means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to astonish, so things that stun are astonishing people.

clue.text: Work performed before makes theatre company scoff

parts.note: rep is short for repertory, a theatre company
to scoff is British slang for eating greedily

explanation.surface: A theatre troupe stuffing their faces makes a revival of an old show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoff' looks like mockery but is slang for eating greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun of a programme or play already broadcast or staged once.
